label: Early original-phase steps (t<=2) on inputs a/c/d (also q,y,u,0,s)
explanation: Mostly fires on the first three original-phase steps: t=1 alone carries 44% of activation mass (25% of t=1 steps are active), and t=0..2 together carry 70%. It is nearly silent from orig_idx 4 on, and never fires on the delimiter or the first copy step. Which token is input strongly gates it. a, c and d are active about 20% of the time (4x lift); restricting to t<=2 with those three tokens gives precision 0.77 but only 0.40 mass recall. Adding q, y, u, 0 and s raises recall at the cost of precision. The strongest activations are c/d/a at step 1-2 after a first token like o or 3. The rest of the mass (about 28%) is spread thinly over copy steps and slightly favours outputs o, z and 3 (6x and 4x lift for o and z), but that clause has precision of only about 0.25. Adding it raises recall but lowers F1, so it is left out. Within t<=2, many steps with other tokens are also weakly active, so recall stays incomplete.
